newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks close higher on blue chip demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks close higher on blue chip demand.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on broad-based buying led by foreign investors, brokers said.
The all share index rose 2.56 points to 580.7, aided by foreign buying of 200,000 John Keells Holdings, which rose two rupees to 177.
"Investors believe the share is cheap at the current price, and has good upside potential," said Gordon Nadesan of brokerage CT Smith.
Alistair Corera of brokerage Forbes & Walker said local institutions also started accumulating shares on expectations that fourth quarter corporate performance would improve.
"Local retailers and institutions were also active," Corera said.
Turnover was an active 46.87 million rupees.
Among actively traded shares were John Keells, Asia Capital and Blue Diamonds Jewellery. Asia Capital rose 50 cents to 7.50 rupees and Blue Diamonds 25 cents to 12.70 rupees.
Brokers said there were signs price gains were supported by volume.
